feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
This is a strong, credible CV with clear senior-level positioning in digital communications, web strategy, and platform operations. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it would be more impactful with sharper outcome-focused achievements, less duplication across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at the National Association of Counties, showing increasing scope, leadership, and responsibility.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: Drupal, analytics, governance, editorial systems, multimedia, and cross-channel communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions: e.g., traffic growth, engagement improvements, efficiency gains, cost savings, campaign results, or adoption metrics.  
- Reduce repetition between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Minor writing/style issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—consider “French (A2, currently learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with one or two concrete differentiators and slightly less overlap with the competencies/skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with seniority and strongest value: enterprise digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of cross-channel leadership and execution.
- Add one contextual qualifier such as “advocacy” or “membership” organizations to better match recent experience.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations, including the workflows, governance, and systems needed to support complex teams. Skilled at stakeholder coordination and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Digital transformation strategy” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Multichannel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication.”
- Prioritize more senior, differentiating strengths: governance, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, editorial operations, and advocacy communications.
- Consider a tighter version: Digital transformation strategy • Multichannel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep style consistent: use “multichannel” (not “multi-channel”) and avoid repeating “workflow” twice.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates the header and Soft Skills section.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten the scope, foreground leadership/ownership, and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, with emphasis on Drupal-based campaigns, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search.”
- Convert duties into 4 concise, results-oriented bullets; start with strong verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Advised,” and add scale/outcomes where possible (site size, users, teams supported, efficiency gains, launch dates).
- Combine overlapping technical points: merge “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with “governance, usability and operational best practices” into one bullet about enterprise communications operations.
- Make the AI-search bullet more concrete: note prototype/launched phase, content corpus, retrieval approach, or expected user benefit.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project list; avoid repeating “AI Hybrid Search” and “We Are Counties Microsite” in full detail here.
- “CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” may duplicate skills sections; keep this role focused on business impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, video production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine the website bullets and keep the strongest numbers: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, reporting improvements, production volume, engagement growth, or efficiency gains from governance and analytics changes.
- Trim generic phrasing like “core digital communications channels” and “improving strategic decision-making”; replace with concrete results or operational scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/newsletter management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and systems built.
- Video leadership overlaps with earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the in-house studio and expanded organizational capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier digital media role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and cross-team coordination at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and front-load outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and specific: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating governance/standards language.
- “Expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; use “launched” or quantify growth if accurate.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy & stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, planning & content design
- Use “content operations” instead of “content leadership” to align with recent experience and sound more concrete.
- Swap “multi-channel” for “cross-channel” and “audience-focused content planning” for “audience strategy, planning & content design” to sound more senior and specific.
- If space is tight, cut “public-sector” or “audience” language here since those themes are already proven elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most important tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items like “jQuery” unless the target role explicitly asks for it.
- Keep the most marketable, recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and API integrations are repeated in Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT,” so this section should emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics infrastructure & insight generation” rather than “Analytics, Insights & Optimization.”
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework development, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger language like “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- If space allows, add outcome-oriented wording: “measurement strategy,” “funnel analysis,” or “performance optimization” to show application.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths, and keep the full tool inventory in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s too generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multimedia details in Technical + IT. Make it sharper by emphasizing operational scope and recent leadership-level capability.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more distinctive phrasing: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and webcast operations • PTZ and studio camera systems • In-house studio management • Hybrid, virtual and live event delivery”
- If space allows, add scale/context rather than task words: e.g., “broadcast-quality” or “enterprise event production” to reflect the NACo studio build and event work.
- Keep nouns consistent across Topline Skills; avoid mixed verb/noun phrasing like “Video production and editing” beside “Studio operations.”
- Consider dropping “editing” unless it’s central to current target roles; leadership/operations is stronger and more recent in this CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item partially duplicates Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); differentiate by focusing on studio/event infrastructure.
- “PTZ camera systems” and studio tooling are also implied in Technical + IT, so avoid overloading both sections with the same wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to sharpen relevance and signal level of expertise, especially around Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: put **Drupal** first and consider adding **advanced** context only to the platforms you’ve used most deeply.
- Consider trimming lower-signal items if they’re not central to target roles, e.g. keep to 3–4 platforms for a stronger, more senior impression.
- If you have evidence, add version/scope in brief elsewhere, e.g. **Drupal 10** or **enterprise/public-sector CMS environments**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus broader capabilities.
- “GitHub Pages” may undersell your seniority unless it directly supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end CMS implementation,” “tagging/measurement deployment,” or “serverless scripting.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use version-specific naming; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more implementation-specific.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want this section focused strictly on coding/build tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software dump and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it more selective and grouped around actual workflow/automation capability.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello | Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning, cross-team coordination”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and systems-building impact; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello.
- Drop lower-signal collaboration tools like Slack and Teams unless this section is meant to include everyday workplace software.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier elsewhere in the CV, e.g., “built workflow systems supporting cross-department communications” rather than listing more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same idea verbatim.
- Basecamp, Slack, Teams, and Trello may feel redundant unless you want to emphasize project-management stack breadth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool list, but it reads as generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email/newsletter operations, this item should better signal scale and platform ownership rather than just naming tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope in brief: Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Mailchimp (email marketing)
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one platform to scale: supported newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Engagement” overlaps with Core Competencies and work experience references to multi-channel communications; keep this item platform-specific.
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale here if it already appears prominently under NACo roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring multimedia outputs, with metrics if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into clearer achievements: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates; and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, website traffic impact, or team/process efficiencies.
- Use stronger verbs than “contributed to” and “high-impact,” e.g., “helped deliver,” “launched,” “scaled,” or “managed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” may feel repetitive with later governance/operations bullets unless you specify what changed.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Cut generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer deliverable such as “produced digital and multimedia content supporting program communications.”
- If possible, add scale or result: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded communications capacity.
- Keep this entry lighter than later NACo roles since stronger digital leadership appears in 2015–2024 positions.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer work; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad digital operations language already covered in 2018–2024 roles.
